Pledge

PLEJ (rhymes with edge) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

a serious promise to do something, often written down or signed

Each student signed a pledge to keep the playground clean.

Worked Example

Marco made a pledge to walk his neighbor's dog every Saturday, and he wrote it on the kitchen calendar.

Marco did not just say 'maybe.' He promised something clear and wrote it down where everyone could see it - that makes it a pledge.

How Pledge Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

promise

promise: saying you will surely do something

commitment

commitment: agreeing to keep doing something

Antonyms

lie

lie: words that are not true

refusal

refusal: saying no to doing something

How Strong Is It? — Offer → pledge → Guarantee

Offer vs. pledge

Offer vs. pledge: Offer is lighter: offering to help is kind, but you can still change your mind.

Guarantee vs. pledge

Guarantee vs. pledge: Guarantee is stronger: a guarantee means the thing will happen for sure, no matter what.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Pledge came into English from an old French word for something valuable you hand over to prove you will keep your word. It is one solid piece, with no smaller parts to break off.

Use the root in a new word: allegiance

Use the root in a new word: allegiance: Every morning the class stands and says the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag.
